Problem: hour_ist and scraped_at_ist are text with a +05:30 offset; date is text
Action: Parsed hour_ist to a timestamp (IST). Kept date, weekday and hour as given.
Why: Needed for weekday/hour grouping and the join to weather.

Problem: All 113,880 hour_ist values carry +05:30; all 102,643 of 102,643 scrape times carry +05:30
Action: No conversion needed: traffic is already in IST.
Why: Same zone as the weather file (see W2), so the join needs no shift.

Problem: Hourly grid is complete (13 routes x 8,760 h = 113,880) but only 102,615 rows are observed; 11,265 rows were not scraped
How_detected: row_status counts; run-length scan per route
Action: Kept the rows on the grid and labelled them in row_status. Analyses use observed rows only.
Why: A complete grid makes gaps visible and joins safe; averages from observed rows only avoid mixing in estimated values.

Problem: Short gaps interpolated: 10,181 rows, longest filled run = 3 h; 28 more rows were scraped but had no duration and got an interpolated duration
How_detected: row_status = interpolated / observed_dur_interpolated; re-interpolated each route and compared
Action: Rule: linear interpolation of duration_min between the nearest observed hours on the same route, only when the gap is <= 3 h (gap_len_h <= 3), rounded to 3 decimals. Re-running this rule reproduces 10,181 of 10,181 interpolated values (max difference 0.0003 min); longest filled gap = 3 h. Gaps > 3 h stay empty (T5).
Why: A 1-3 hour hole barely changes a smooth daily curve; longer holes would invent traffic.
Status: Confirmed from the data (rule worked out from the data; the upstream cleaning script is not in the repo)

Problem: 1,056 rows left empty in 41 runs of more than 3 h: all 13 routes on 2026-02-06 (312 rows), one route for 437 h (23 May - 11 Jun 2026), another for 137 h (01 Oct - 06 Oct 2025), the rest scattered
Action: Not filled; duration, speed and congestion are blank.
Why: Filling a whole day or multi-week stretch would fabricate a pattern. Excluded by the observed-only rule.

Problem: Duplicate (route, hour) keys; duplicate (route, scrape time) readings
How_detected: duplicated() on (route_code, hour_ist) and on (route_code, scraped_at_ist)
Action: Rule: one row per route per hour; if two readings fall in the same hour keep one (PySpark step 3 collapses any duplicates). Checked, none found.
Why: Grid is unique by construction.

Problem: Flat-lined duration: the same value repeated (174 rows on 4 routes)
How_detected: qa_flag = flatline; run-length of identical duration_min over consecutive observed hours
Action: Rule: flag when the same duration_min repeats for >= 6 consecutive observed hours on one route. This reproduces 167 of 174 flags, and every run of >= 6 (167 rows) is flagged; the other 7 flagged rows sit in shorter runs (3-5 h) that this rule does not explain. Flagged and kept. Max effect on any heatmap cell if removed: 0.002 index points.
Why: Likely a stuck reading, but removing it changes nothing visible.
Status: Confirmed from the data (rule worked out from the data; the upstream cleaning script is not in the repo)

Problem: Google returned a longer alternate route: 6,079 rows, median distance 11.4 km vs 10.2 km normal; most on Sarjapur Road and Hosur Road. Detours: 28 rows
Action: Flagged and kept. Removing all flagged rows moves any heatmap cell by at most 0.044 index points (mean 0.011).
Why: A longer route inflates duration and so the congestion index; the effect is too small to change any finding, so rows stay in for full coverage.

Problem: Extreme congestion: 776 rows. 183 of them (24%) fall in an hour when 3 or more routes spike together; only 56 fall on a holiday, festival or long-weekend date
How_detected: qa_flag = extreme_event; breadth by hour; calendar join
Action: Kept and flagged as real events. Top dates are listed on the Evidence_Events sheet, with the metro daily total as a second source.
Why: A sensor fault would hit one route; city-wide simultaneous spikes are real. Most are NOT explained by the holiday calendar, so the calendar is incomplete (for example 1 Jan 2026).

Problem: duration_z is a per-route z-score (every route has mean 0, sd 1: True); duration_minmax is 0-1 per route
Action: Used duration_z for the normalised chart (Figure 3). The heatmap uses the raw congestion index.
Why: Routes differ in length (9-39 km), so minutes are not comparable across routes; z-scores per route are.

Problem: Embedded AccuWeather columns are 83.5% empty (temp, realfeel, humidity, rsi_flag, aqi)
Action: Not used. Rain comes from the Open-Meteo file, which has no gaps.
Why: A column that is 84% blank cannot support an hourly analysis.

Problem: speed = distance / duration holds (max error 0.002 km/h); congestion_index = duration / free-flow holds (max error 0.001)
Action: Checked, none found.
Why: Derived columns can be trusted.

Problem: speed_kmph ranges 5.9-59.0 km/h; duration_min <= 0 on 0 rows
How_detected: Range check: speed < 3 or > 80 km/h, duration <= 0
Action: Rule: a reading is invalid if speed < 3 km/h or > 80 km/h (above the city limit on any of these roads) or duration <= 0. None found, nothing removed.
Why: Impossible speeds would mean a bad scrape; all values are plausible for city traffic.

Problem: distance_km ranges 9.2-38.6 km; ratio to the route's median distance is <= 1.10 on unflagged observed rows, 1.10-1.42 on alt_route rows and >= 1.53 on detour rows
How_detected: distance_km / median observed distance_km of the route
Action: Rule (observed rows only; interpolated rows inherit a neighbour's distance and are not flagged): ratio > 1.10 -> alt_route; ratio > 1.5 -> detour (the gap between 1.42 and 1.53 in the data means any cut-off in that range gives the same flags). Flagged and kept (see T8).
Why: A different distance means Google routed the trip differently, so the duration is not comparable to the usual route.

Problem: timestamp is text with no zone marker
Action: Parsed to a timestamp; hour, date and weekday columns verified against it (all match).
Why: Needed for the join to traffic.

Problem: Files carry no time zone. Mean temperature peaks at hour 13 (Aug-Sep 2025) and 14 (Oct 2025-Sep 2026) and is lowest at hour 5 and 4; humidity peaks at hour 5 and 5
How_detected: Diurnal cycle test (hour of daily temperature maximum)
Action: Treated timestamps as IST: a UTC clock would peak near hour 8-9, not 13-14. No conversion applied. The SQL table also names the column timestamp_ist.
Why: The data confirm local time. The files do not show the conversion itself: the brief wants it shown, so attach the Open-Meteo request (timezone=Asia/Kolkata) or the UTC-to-IST code.
Status: Needs teammate confirmation (show the API call or conversion code)

Problem: Weather joins traffic on (route, hour): 113,880 of 113,880 traffic rows matched
Action: No action needed.
Why: Each of the 13 routes has its own nearby weather point (13 locations).

Problem: Nulls and duplicate (route, hour) keys; rain vs precipitation
Rows_affected: 0 nulls, 0 duplicates; rain = precipitation on 132,912 of 132,912 rows
Action: Checked, none found. Used rain (precipitation is identical).
Why: Complete hourly record from the API.

Problem: rain_status = Rainy when rain >= 0.1 mm in the hour (every Non-Rainy hour is 0.0); 16.4% of hours in the traffic window and 39.0% in Aug-Sep 2025 are Rainy
Action: Kept as is. The rain chart defines a rainy evening as any rainy hour between 18:00 and 21:00 on that route and also splits by season.
Why: 0.1 mm is the API's smallest unit, so drizzle counts as rain. Rain is also seasonal (most rainy evenings fall in Jun-Sep), so season is controlled.

Problem: File is semicolon-separated and station names contain commas; Date is text
How_detected: Parser error on a comma split; head of file
Action: Read with sep=';' and parsed Date. Stations: 83, names consistent, no stray spaces.
Why: A comma parse mis-splits names like 'Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Station, Vidhana Soudha'.

Problem: No zone in the file; Date + Hour only
How_detected: Morning peak sits at hours 8-9 at residential stations
Action: Treated as IST; no conversion.
Why: The values are already local clock time.

Problem: Entries and exits were merged on (Date, Hour, Station): 92,280 rows. Boardings match the original file on every row; exits match on every row
How_detected: Compared with the repo's separate files
Action: Kept. 2 exit riders in the 3,336 absent station-hours were dropped by the merge (2 of 33,727,301).
Why: Merged layout is what the team wanted; the loss is immaterial.
Status: Confirmed against the repo's raw files (separate check)

Problem: 15 Yellow Line stations (BTM Layout, Beratena Agrahara, Biocon Hebbagodi and 12 more) opened on 10 Aug 2025. Before that they have no rows for 3,336 station-hours (139 station-days)
How_detected: Expected grid vs rows; first day with daytime riders per station
Action: Excluded these 15 stations from the weekday comparison so the 68 stations open all period are compared like for like.
Why: Public riders start on 11 Aug 2025. The few earlier riders (180 riders in 24 station-hours at 6 stations, 3-9 Aug) may be final testing; not confirmed.

Problem: 13 whole days absent: 19-31 Aug 2025 (the repo's RTI data stops at 18 Aug and restarts 1 Sep)
Action: Not filled. Ganesh Chaturthi (27 Aug) therefore has no hourly metro data; the daily ticket file does have it.
Why: A whole-day gap cannot be filled honestly.

Problem: Negative values: 0. Largest hourly value 4,425. Station-days with total 0: 0. Repeated identical non-zero values in consecutive hours: 212 (of these 6 are 10 riders or fewer)
How_detected: min/max; all-zero day check; run scan
Action: Checked. Repeats are small counts (chance), not stuck readings. No rows removed.
Why: No sign of a failed sensor.

Problem: 18,200 zero rows: 18,020 in closed hours (23:00-05:59); 180 in daytime, of which 158 are Yellow Line stations on or before the 10 Aug 2025 opening
How_detected: Zero count by hour and station
Action: Overnight zeros kept (real). Zeros at the Yellow Line stations up to opening kept, not flagged. The other 22 daytime zeros kept and flagged.
Why: The remaining few cannot be told apart from a true zero or an outage.

Problem: Extreme station-hours (robust z > 6 and > 200 riders): 581; clustered on 15 Aug (303), 05 Sep (48), 08 Aug (39)
How_detected: Median/MAD per station x hour x weekday/weekend
Action: Kept and flagged. 15 Aug and 5 Sep are public holidays; the other dates are not in the calendar and their cause is unverified.
Why: They cluster on a few dates across many stations, which looks like real events, not failure.

Problem: Riders recorded at hour 3 (service closed): 30 rows at 9 stations, mostly Majestic, Yeshwantpur and the KSR railway station on Mondays
Action: Kept and flagged.
Why: Possibly test runs of the metro before service; the actual cause is not known.

Problem: Boardings total 33,837,882 vs exits total 33,727,299 (0.33% apart)
How_detected: Sum comparison; daily gap peaks at 2.4% on 15 Aug
Action: Not reconciled. Boardings are the main measure; exits only describe flow direction.
Why: Riders may not scan or tap in or out (for example token users), and staff let passengers through during gate faults. The actual cause is not known.

Problem: Raw tracker file uses dd-mm-yyyy; the final file uses yyyy-mm-dd
Action: Final file already ISO; parsed with 0 unparseable dates. Day of Week verified against the date (all match).
Why: Avoids day/month swaps.

Problem: BMRCL does not publish every day: 197 of 476 calendar days missing between 01 Aug 2025 and 19 Nov 2026; 146 of the 365 days inside the traffic window. Longest runs: 04 Oct-21 Oct 2026 (18 d), 09 Sep-19 Sep 2026 (11 d), 21 Sep-01 Oct 2026 (11 d)
How_detected: Date range vs the full calendar
Action: Not filled. Weekday averages use available days only.
Why: Ridership cannot be estimated for a missing day without hiding the gap.

Problem: Traffic Band puts Monday with Tue/Wed (Early Week) and Friday with Thursday (Mid Week)
How_detected: Crosstab of Day of Week x Traffic Band
Action: Not used for the Mon/Fri comparison; weekday computed from the date instead.
Why: The band hides exactly the Monday and Friday difference the question asks about.

Problem: Three identities checked on every row: Smart Cards = Stored Value + One-day + Three-day + Five-day; Total QR = NammaMetro + WhatsApp + Paytm + ONDC; Total = Smart Cards + Tokens + NCMC + Group + Total QR. Failures: 0, 0, 0 of 279 rows
Action: Checked, none found. Total QR includes ONDC (four channels), as confirmed by the team.
Why: Confirms the Total used in Figure 5 is built correctly.

Problem: QR ONDC is 0 on all 237 days before 12 Aug 2026 and above 0 on every day from then on: it is a payment method introduced on that date
How_detected: First non-zero date; zero check before it
Action: Kept as 0.
Why: QR ONDC started appearing on that date, when it was introduced as a payment method.

Problem: 15 Dec 2025 repeats 11 Dec 2025 exactly on seven columns (Tokens, NCMC, Group, Total QR and three QR channels)
Action: Excluded 15 Dec 2025 from the daily charts.
Why: Stale carry-forward: the smart-card columns differ, so the date is real but the rest is a copy.

Problem: 17 Jul 2026 shows Total Tokens = 24,573 (typical 190,000-300,000)
Action: Kept as published and used in the charts. Cannot be corrected without the source.
Why: The team decided to keep the value. Total still adds up (D4). The low tokens pull that Friday down.

Problem: Daily Total rises from mid-Aug 2026: Tue-Thu median 935,587 in Jul vs 1,090,847 from 17 Aug to 19 Nov (+17%); it builds through early Aug and holds into Oct-Nov (Tue-Thu median 1,084,609)
Action: Kept as a real change in ridership. Figure 5 uses the full data; its footnote shows how little the change moves the weekday indices.
Why: Team: the Yellow Line added another train on 15 Aug. The rise starts earlier than that, so it is not explained by that alone; cause not verified.

Problem: 10 unusually low days (robust z < -3.5 within weekday); 7 are public holidays; high days on 14 Aug 2026 and 29 Apr 2026 also spike on the roads
Action: Kept and flagged as real events.
Why: Holiday dips and the road/metro co-spikes point to real behaviour, not failure.

Problem: No missing days: 365 daily rows (traffic, 1 Oct 2025-30 Sep 2026) and 61 (metro, 1 Aug-30 Sep 2025); no duplicates
Action: Checked, none found.
Why: Daily series are complete.

Problem: interest_index is not a whole number on 79% (traffic) and 43% (metro) of days, although Google gives integers 0-100
Action: Kept as numeric. The scaling or stitching method is not recorded in the file.
Why: Non-integers show the series was rescaled or averaged; the method belongs in the source register.
Status: Needs teammate confirmation (document the scaling method)

Problem: interest_z (mean 0, sd 1) and interest_minmax (0-1) added per term; the index is relative to the term's own peak
Action: Used interest_z against the traffic z-score in Figure 3. Never compare raw index values across terms.
Why: Trends has no units; z-scores put it on the same scale as congestion.

Problem: flag_spike marks 21 traffic days and 4 metro days; the metro spike (9-12 Aug 2025) coincides with the Yellow Line opening (10-11 Aug 2025)
Action: Kept and flagged as real events.
Why: Matches an independent source. Spike rule is not recorded.

Problem: 476 days, 1 Aug 2025-19 Nov 2026, no gaps or duplicates; 28 public holidays, 30 long-weekend days; blanks in holiday_name are normal
Action: Checked, none found. Used to separate holidays from ordinary days.
Why: Covers every other table. It misses some real events (e.g. 1 Jan 2026): see T9.

Problem: Metro hourly covers Aug-Sep 2025 only; traffic covers Oct 2025-Sep 2026. They share no hours.
Action: Road-vs-metro comparison is made at weekday level on shared dates only (Figure 5); no hourly road-vs-metro join.
Why: Joining on non-overlapping periods would be meaningless.
